description: English behavioral questions in the big-tech STAR style. Every follow-up probes for specifics: numbers, decisions, and what you actually changed.

questions.question: Tell me about a project you are most proud of. What was your specific contribution, and what would have happened without you?
questions.follow_up: Give me the number that proves impact. If you did not measure it, how would you measure it next time?

questions.question: Describe a time you disagreed with your manager or a senior engineer. How did you handle it, and what was the outcome?
questions.follow_up: What did you learn about when to push back and when to commit? What signal told you it was time to stop arguing?

questions.question: Tell me about your biggest professional failure. Not a disguised success story — a real failure.
questions.follow_up: What did you change in your own behavior afterwards? Concretely, not 'I learned to communicate better'.

questions.question: Describe a time you had to deliver with a deadline you believed was impossible.
questions.follow_up: Walk me through what you cut and what you refused to cut. Who did you negotiate with, and what did you trade?

questions.question: Tell me about a time you influenced a decision without having any formal authority.
questions.follow_up: Who resisted you the most, and what was their legitimate concern? How did you address it instead of overriding it?

questions.question: Describe a situation where you had to make a call with incomplete data and the cost of waiting was high.
questions.follow_up: What was the worst-case scenario of your call? What was your rollback plan if it went wrong?

questions.question: Tell me about a time you received harsh or unfair feedback. What did you do in the following two weeks?
questions.follow_up: Which part of the feedback turned out to be right after all? Which part did you consciously decide not to act on?

questions.question: Describe a time you fixed something that was technically 'not your job'.
questions.follow_up: How did you balance this against your actual deliverables? Did your manager know, and should they have?

questions.question: Tell me about a conflict between two teammates that you helped resolve.
questions.follow_up: What did each side want that the other side did not understand? Did you solve the problem or just the relationship?

questions.question: Describe the most technically difficult problem you have solved. Take me through your reasoning from symptom to root cause.
questions.follow_up: What were your two dead-end hypotheses, and what evidence killed each of them?

questions.question: Tell me about a time you pushed back on a customer or stakeholder request that you believed was wrong for the product.
questions.follow_up: How did you distinguish 'customer is wrong' from 'I am wrong'? What compromise did you end up making?

questions.question: Why this role, and why now? Connect it to specific things you have done, not generic enthusiasm.
questions.follow_up: What is the strongest counter-argument to your own motivation — the reason you might leave in 18 months?
